title: Conditional Complier Effects under Weak Compliance with an Auxiliary Instrument-Only Cohort
banked_reason: Clean D0.5 math and decision PASS; achieved subfield below required field, paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, salvageable false; independent validity gate found no bounded same-scope repair.
gap_reasons: Its scope remains a known scalar uniform design, binary records and one fixed smoothness triple, with no adaptation or characterization across dimensions and regularity regimes.
The calibration threshold establishes an order benchmark, while the conservative constants and Markov intervals do not establish practically useful finite-sample registry sizes.

These substantive scope and operational limits constrain the projected paper score even after competent rewriting; the delivered package does not establish a broadly applicable framework or resolve a recognized general open problem.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched original-record minimax squared-risk and finite honest connected-interval frontiers, closed the current-label-excluded information bottleneck, and evaluated the consistency and oracle-calibration thresholds. Final mathematical and decision panels passed with no findings after citation verification and comparator repairs; the independent terminal-validity consult found no bounded same-scope root fix. The result achieved subfield rather than the required field floor and stopped before F1, so these are audited informal proofs with no Lean formalization or F7 promotion.
tldr:
The finite minimax root squared error and honest connected-interval length for the stated conditional complier effect both have order
\(\min\{1,\max\{(n\delta^2)^{-1/3},[n(n+m)\delta^6]^{-1/7}\}\}\).
The independent compatible cohort contains instrument labels but no uptake or outcomes. Each IV marginal belongs to the KBRW observed-regression model; the full IV experiment is distinct. At fixed strength without calibration, the \(n^{-2/7}\) difficulty persists inside a verified full-support monotone-IV subclass. Shrinking compliance and assignment-only calibration yield the matched two-resource phase diagram. In the shrinking-oracle regime, supplied-propensity precision is recovered exactly in order when \(n+m\gtrsim n^{4/3}\delta^{-4/3}\), while main responses remain necessary.
gap: Published conditional-LATE learners retain positive first-stage or oracle-learner assumptions. Existing conditional-covariance and semisupervised average-effect results do not directly determine the exact joint pointwise risk, finite honest length and necessary calibration budget in this shrinking-compliance principal-type experiment.
fill: The joint frontier in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:joint-frontier} pairs total finite projection procedures with lawful full-data testing alternatives. Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:resource-consistency} converts that frontier into consistency conditions and a necessary and sufficient registry budget.
